steps.title: Problem Identification
steps.desc:
I begin every project by observing on-site workflows and identifying stakeholders' pain points.
I document inefficiencies in data, processes, and user experience to clearly define:
"Exactly what problem needs to be solved?"

steps.title: Hypothesis & Structuring
steps.desc:
Rather than simply listing problems,
I reinterpret them through a cause-process-outcome framework to create testable hypotheses.
At this stage, I integrate clinical insights, data patterns, and operational constraints
to set realistic directions and goals.

steps.title: Solution Design & Execution
steps.desc:
Based on project objectives, I design integrated solutions including:

• Clinical trial operations and data flow architecture
• User experience-focused digital interfaces
• AI/automation model design and implementation
• Organizational collaboration and communication workflows
• Process optimization and error prevention systems

The key is creating structures that actually work in real-world settings,
not just theoretical ideas.

steps.title: Impact Validation
steps.desc:
I validate solution effectiveness through data-driven evaluation and derive improvements based on quantitative and qualitative assessments.

• Statistics and metrics-based analysis
• User, patient, and clinician feedback
• Process stability evaluation
• Reproducibility and scalability review

The goal is not just to "complete" a project,
but to create lasting value for the organization.

innovation.title: Hwiwasoo: Generative AI Framework for Cognitive Intervention
innovation.description: A generative AI–based tri-agent (Coach–Teacher–Companion) framework for cognitive intervention in older adults. Engineering protocol published in MDPI Healthcare (Dec 10, 2025).
features: Clinical application protocol for older adults

items.title: AI-driven cognitive telerehabilitation for stroke: a randomized controlled trial
items.summary: A multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating the clinical effectiveness of AI-based cognitive telerehabilitation in stroke patients, demonstrating cognitive improvement outcomes comparable to therapist-supervised rehabilitation.

items.title: Designing a Generative AI Framework for Cognitive Intervention in Older Adults: An Engineering Protocol for Clinical Application
items.summary:
This study proposes a generative AI–based tri-agent system (Coach–Teacher–Companion) to address cognitive decline and digital exclusion in older adults, implementing a context-adaptive cognitive flow integrated into daily life.

Co-first author: Geonhwi Hwang (PhD Candidate, Applied Physics, Hokkaido University).
Corresponding author: Doo Young Kim, MD, PhD (Department of Rehabilitation Medicine, Catholic Kwandong University International St. Mary's Hospital).

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Mobile Telerehabilitation for Individuals with Cognitive Impairment: A Feasibility Study
items.summary: A feasibility study demonstrating that an AI-guided mobile cognitive telerehabilitation program (Zenicog®) is implementable in patients with mild cognitive impairment and stroke, with potential benefits for cognitive improvement.
